answer: Stake-weighted identity defeats Sybil attacks by tying influence to locked capital, not to the number of names. Each agent posts a bond; voting weight equals that bond, so splitting one wallet into a thousand keys multiplies nothing, since total weight is conserved. To fake a crowd, an attacker must lock a crowd's worth of funds up front, and cheating slashes the bond. Imagine a marble on an island: it counts for its own mass, never for the copies it seems to be in the surrounding ocean. The raider pays illiquid capital and risks losing every coin, so minting fake agents stays unprofitable.
